recentItems.title: Israel bars Arab parties and candidates from election, Ofer Cassif calls ban unlawful
recentItems.description:
Israel’s Central Elections Committee voted to disqualify the United Arab List and the Joint List from next month’s elections. It also banned candidates Sami Abu Shehadeh and Ofer Cassif, accusing them of supporting terror and denying Israel as a Jewish state. The Joint List says Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and far-right Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir are trying to discourage 1.2 million Palestinian citizens of Israel from voting. The decisions need final approval by Israel’s Supreme Court. Ofer Cassif told Al Jazeera the move was predictable, unlawful and politically motivated. He rejected allegations of supporting armed struggle, saying he and his colleagues have always opposed violence and supported non-violent struggle. Cassif said the attorney general opposed the disqualifications and found no legal basis, arguing that politicians should not have the power to disqualify other politicians. He said he is confident the Supreme Court will overturn the bans and warned that Israel would become a “fully-fledged fascist dictatorship” if they stand.

recentItems.title: Toxic smoke from Indonesia fires spreads across Southeast Asia
recentItems.description:
Indonesia is battling widespread forest fires that have blanketed Borneo and neighbouring countries in toxic haze, worsened by an unusually severe El Nino weather pattern. Officials say 12.5 million people have been affected by smoke-related illnesses, with schools shifting online and clinics reporting a surge in respiratory cases. The Philippines, Malaysia and Singapore have also felt the effects of the drifting haze. Authorities have deployed firefighters and pledged to prosecute those responsible for illegal burning, though data shows more forest has been cleared this year than in previous seasons.

Al Jazeera’s Rob McBride reports from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

Rohingya in Bangladesh preserve documents and memories of Myanmar in digital archive
recentItems.description:
Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh's Cox's Bazar are digitising family photographs, identity papers and land deeds to preserve proof of their heritage. More than a million fled persecution in Myanmar since 2017, and archivists hope the encrypted, decentralised collection will safeguard cultural memory for younger generations while potentially serving as evidence in ongoing ICC and ICJ cases against Myanmar. Many refugees also see the documents as vital for any future repatriation process.

Al Jazeera’s Tanvir Chowdhury reports from Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh.

recentItems.title: How Israel's UNRWA ban is affecting education and healthcare in Gaza
recentItems.description:
UNRWA has long provided education, healthcare and aid to Palestinians in Gaza, but Israeli restrictions have left much of its network non-functional. Before the war, 300,000 children attended 288 UNRWA-run schools; many now shelter displaced families instead. Of 22 healthcare centres once operating across the Strip, only six remain active, leaving patients with chronic illnesses struggling to access medicine. The agency says it can no longer bring in aid independently, relying instead on international partners for supplies.

Al Jazeera’s Tareq Abu Azzoum reports from Khan Younis, Gaza.

recentItems.title: Gaza $2.45 billion reconstruction plan. Who decides its future?
recentItems.description:
Gaza now has a $2.45bn six-month recovery plan, from housing and hospitals to security and 4G. But major questions remain over Israeli withdrawal, Hamas’s disarmament and how much control Palestinians will have. 

Al Jazeera's Noor Wazwaz explains.

recentItems.title: Colombia deploys troops after armed group strike shuts Santa Marta
recentItems.description:
The Colombian government says businesses are beginning to reopen in the Caribbean city of Santa Marta, after a 48-hour strike imposed by the armed group - ACSN. 
The shutdown was in retaliation for a security operation that killed one of the group’s top commanders.

Al Jazeera’s Alessandro Rampietti reports from Bogota, Colombia.
